greeting: Good morning, Rick! Happy Saturday, grab a coffee and enjoy a relaxed scroll through today's tech news.

items.title: YouTube could pay $3 billion to settle social media addiction lawsuits with school districts
items.note: YouTube may pay around $3 billion to thousands of US school districts that say the app hurts students' mental health. The deal would also add new safety features for teens, something every former teacher can appreciate.

items.title: iOS 27 lets you use two iPhones with the same phone number
items.note: A handy change in iOS 27: if you carry two iPhones, you can now keep the same phone number on both. Calls and texts follow you to whichever one you pick up.

items.title: Best Apple Black Friday deals now live: AirPods, MacBook Neo, Series 12, M6 MacBook Pro, more [Updated]
items.note: Black Friday sales are already live, and 9to5Mac rounded up the best Apple deals in one spot. AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Max 2, and Apple Watch Series 12 are at some of their lowest prices yet.

items.title: Google Gemini Partners With Watch Duty to Clear Static From Firefighter Radio
items.note: Google's Gemini team spent six months working with the wildfire app Watch Duty to clean up static on firefighter radio calls. It's a nice example of AI doing real good when it counts.

items.title: New Hyundai Elantra Hybrid Debuts With 53 Mpg, AI in the Dash
items.note: Hyundai showed off a redesigned Elantra Hybrid at the LA Auto Show that aims for about 53 mpg. It also gets a new AI voice assistant and one-pedal driving like an electric car.

items.title: Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Officially Heading to Mars
items.note: NASA's twin Mars probes, nicknamed Blue and Gold, spent a year looping near Earth and just used a flyby to slingshot toward the red planet. No space agency has tried staging a Mars trip like this before.

items.title: Teenage Engineering's first CD player kind of looks like a turntable
items.note: Teenage Engineering made a $329 CD player where the disc spins right on top like a record. A fun, retro gadget for anyone who still has a stack of CDs in the closet.

items.title: Google rolls out new search homepage with AI chat history and no search button
items.note: The Google.com homepage you've used for years is getting a makeover with AI chat built right in, and the classic search button is gone. Here's what you'll see next time you open it.
